title: Polish Plural: Rules, Endings and Irregular Nouns
excerpt: Polish plural rules made simple: -y, -i, -e and -a endings, the masculine-personal plural (studenci, Polacy), irregulars and pięć kotów.
metaDescription: The Polish plural explained: -y, -i, -e and -a endings, masculine-personal forms like studenci and Polacy, irregular nouns, drzwi and okulary, and pięć kotów.
summary: The Polish plural has only two genders: masculine-personal (male people and mixed groups) and everything else.
Feminine and non-personal masculine nouns take -y, -i (after k, g) or -e (soft stems); neuter nouns take -a, with dziecko → dzieci as the big exception.
Masculine-personal nouns change their final consonant (student → studenci, Polak → Polacy) or take -owie or -e, and adjectives and past-tense verbs agree (dobrzy studenci byli).
Nouns such as drzwi, okulary and urodziny exist only in the plural, and after numbers 5 and up the noun goes into the genitive plural (pięć kotów, pięć książek).
